records.source: No published Starship main-tank vent geometry was found; SpaceX broadcast imagery shows venting from the ship's forward and aft sections without a measurable station.
records.variant: Starship main-tank (LOX/CH4) vent used by the Flight 14 return main-tank vent
records.conditions: An on-axis point 8.0 m forward of the part centre (forward main-tank dome region), exhausting forward along +Y, with no exit area. It only places the vented mass's outlet for variable-mass transport; the vent produces no thrust in the model.
records.uncertainty: Station +/-8 m along the axis; real vents are on the hull and may discharge laterally, which this axisymmetric point omits.

records.source: No published Starship V3 main-tank vent geometry was found.
records.conditions: On-axis point 8.0 m forward of the part centre, exhausting along +Y, no exit area; transport geometry only, no thrust.
records.uncertainty: Station +/-8 m; lateral hull discharge omitted.

records.source: Exosphere part data: every engine part places its thrust point at its aft end (thrust_position_y_m = -length/2) and stacks it at the vehicle's published length. Verified for the AS-506 F-1 against the MSFC/Boeing drawing 'Saturn V Apollo Flight Configuration' (bottom of F-1 engines at X-station -115.36 in, the model's skirt datum).
records.variant: Engine exit-plane station for variable-mass transport
records.conditions: An engine's exit plane is its mount's thrust point moved back by the model's nozzleExitAxialOffsetM (zero unless declared); an exit with no declared diameter is a point outlet. RCS outlets are the declared nozzle points; a stuck-thruster outlet is its declared thruster's nozzle.
records.uncertainty: A point outlet omits the exit-disk term m_dot*a^2/4*(E+n n^T): under 0.1 % of an S-IC engine's pitch flux moment, but it removes axial-spin transport (m_dot*a^2/2).

records.source: Continuity identity d(sum m c)/dt = p_rel - sum q e (Reynolds transport); NASA/CR-1998-208246 (Eke), sections 3.2 and 4.3, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19980210404/downloads/19980210404.pdf
records.variant: Feed path from each store's loss point to its outlet
records.conditions: Flow leaves a settled column at its free surface (a fixed-shape store at its centroid), runs inside the tank to its floor, then straight to the exit; open outlets share their feed group's store outflow by weight. p_rel = sum q (e - t) satisfies continuity exactly; h_rel = sum q [(t - c) x (b - c) + (b - c) x (e - c)] depends on the straight-duct route. Across a flow change P = m v_material + R p_rel and H = I omega + h_rel are continuous.
records.uncertainty: Real feed lines bend and swirl is not modelled; h_rel cancels for symmetric clusters and is small for single off-axis outlets. Instantaneous flow changes stand in for finite valve transients with the same total impulse.
